examples.prompt: You are stuck in an endless cycle of whenever you die, you will resurrect as a different person in another world and the only way to break the cycle and return home is by destroying the world you are in. The problem? A prophesied hero or group of heroes always rise up to ruin your plans.
examples.response: I raise my blade to shatter the sky above this endless world, knowing that my death will only spawn a new hero to stop me. A golden light erupts from the crowd as the prophesied savior steps forward, their armor gleaming with the very power I sought to destroy. My sword snaps in their hands, and the cycle resets, sending me reborn in a realm where the stars are made of obsidian. I scream in frustration as the familiar face of another hero appears, ready to repeat the dance of destruction and salvation. The universe spins on, indifferent to my eternal struggle, as I prepare to die again for the thousandth time.

examples.prompt: Tailor me a story of what it means to be human.
examples.response: I feel the sharp sting of salt on my skin as I cry over a loss that feels too heavy to carry alone. My hands tremble when I reach for the cup, reminding me that my strength is fragile and fleeting. I laugh at a joke that isn't funny, just because the warmth of connection matters more than the truth. I choose to forgive someone who hurt me, not because they deserve it, but because I want to be free of the weight. In this messy, broken, and beautiful moment, I understand that being human is simply the act of trying anyway.

examples.prompt: A new rule on Earth is made which allows everyone to legally kill 1 person in their life, this affects the world severely & changes how everybody acts.
examples.response: The moment the law takes effect, the air grows heavy with the weight of a single, inevitable choice hanging over every heart. People stop rushing to work or school, instead standing frozen on street corners, eyes darting as they scan the crowds for their destined target. A young man finally breaks the silence, raising a gun not with rage, but with a terrifying, hollow calm, and fires at a stranger who looks back with equal resignation. The world holds its breath as the shot rings out, shattering the illusion of safety and revealing the fragile thread that binds us all. In the sudden quiet that follows, humanity realizes that while they gained the right to end a life, they have lost the very thing that makes living meaningful.
